material_finding.observed: The retained Trigger-1 workflow validates the canonical atomic claim, records TRIGGER1_SOURCE_HEAD/TREE and checks claim-main ancestry before intervention. The retained compatibility launcher independently requires a clean Git identity and checks pre/post source stability, but on the observed main it does not bind that pre-intervention identity back to the workflow-recorded lease source. Its new defense-in-depth guard blocks GitHub Actions runs when TRIGGER1_LEASE_ADMITTED is absent, while direct non-GitHub launcher invocation remains outside that workflow guard.
material_finding.risk: A clean checkout could change between workflow lease admission and launcher source measurement, remain stable thereafter, and produce internally consistent pre/post evidence for a different source than the workflow-bound source. Direct invocation can also bypass the workflow-only lease gate unless the launcher itself revalidates the canonical claim before model intervention.
material_finding.counterhypothesis: Workflow lease admission plus launcher pre/post stability are sufficient because the checkout is expected not to change between steps.
material_finding.falsifier: An explicit lease-to-pre-source equality/revalidation check eliminates the gap; without it, the two evidence islands remain separately self-consistent.
